translations.source_sense_description: кукла в рост человека для демонстрации одежды

glosses: A dummy, or life-size model of the human body, used for the fitting or displaying of clothes.

examples.text: At the same time, Mr. Bolton was intrigued by Mr. Sundsbo’s proposal to make models look like mannequins because it spoke to the blurring of boundaries — between good and evil, angels and demons, nature and technology, permanence and decay — that was a consistent theme of the McQueen collections.
There was a time when a mannequin was the sculptural equivalent of fashion model. Like a fashion model, the mannequin was intended to reflect our social, professional and aesthetic aspirations.
With the idea that guests may feel lonely eating at a restaurant that can only reach 50% capacity[…]the restaurant will be placing mannequins throughout its dining rooms.

glosses: A jointed model of the human body used by artists, especially to demonstrate the arrangement of drapery.
An anatomical model of the human body for use in teaching of e.g. CPR.
A person who models clothes.

examples.text: […]all of which made a perfect neutral background for the mannequins who moved around swiftly, gracefully, exhibiting one glorious creation after another.

glosses: A silent person; a person who does not talk.

examples.text:
The man's name […] was engraved in the centre, and beneath this, written in ink with the same elaborate precision as the engraving, there was a brief message.
I am a deaf-mute, but I read the lips and understand what is said to me. Please do not shout.
 […] Singer looked very carefully at his lips when he spoke—he had noticed that before. But a dummy!

glosses: A stupid person.

examples.text: Don't be such a dummy!

glosses: A term of address.

examples.text: Hey dummy, what's good wit chu?

glosses: A figure of a person or animal used by a ventriloquist; a puppet.
Something constructed with the size and form of a human, to be used in place of a person.

examples.text: To understand the effects of the accident, we dropped a dummy from the rooftop.

glosses: A person who is the mere tool of another; a man of straw.
A deliberately nonfunctional device or tool used in place of a functional one.

examples.text: The hammer and drill in the display are dummies.

examples.text: The baby wants her dummy.

glosses: A player whose hand is shown and is to be played from by another player.
A word serving only to make a construction grammatical.

examples.text: The pronoun "it" in "It's a mystery why this happened" is a dummy.

glosses: An unused parameter or value.

examples.text: If flag1 is false, the other parameters are dummies.

glosses: A feigned pass or kick or play in order to deceive an opponent.
A bodily gesture meant to fool an opposing player; a feint.

examples.text: Raul Meireles was the victim of the home side's hustling on this occasion giving the ball away to the impressive David Vaughan who slipped in Taylor-Fletcher. The striker sold Daniel Agger with the best dummy of the night before placing his shot past keeper Pepe Reina.

glosses: A newborn animal that is indifferent to stimulus and does not voluntarily move.

examples.text: a dummy calf, lamb, or foal

glosses: A fairy chess piece that cannot move or capture, but can be captured and used to skip moving another piece.

examples.text: In Monochromatic chess moves are only allowed between cells of the same colour. Thus the kings are reduced to ferses, the rooks to dabbabariders, and the knights to dummies. glosses: To make a mock-up or prototype version of something, without some or all off its intended functionality.

examples.text: The carpenters dummied some props for the rehearsals.

glosses: To feint.

glosses: Extremely.

examples.text: Leonardo da Vinci chose a 15th century criminal as a model for Judas in his painting The Last Supper.

glosses: A person, usually an attractive male or female, who is hired to show items or goods to the public, such as items that are given away as prizes on a TV game show.
A representation of a physical object.

examples.text: The boy played with a model of a World War II fighter plane.

examples.text: The sculptor modelled the clay into the form of a dolphin.
